newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brittan urges Danes to back EU on US anti-Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: Brittan urges Danes to back EU on US anti-Cuba law.

text.p: European Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan urged Denmark on Thursday to fall back into line with the other 14 European Union member states in their joint stand against U.S. anti-Cuba trade laws.

"I hope our Danish colleagues will help us reach a position by unanimity, which is needed to react," Brittan said at a lunch at a European forum in Paris. "I understand the Danish problem but I have to say I hope Denmark will reconsider its position in the coming days."
Denmark said on Tuesday it would veto planned EU retaliatory measures against the U.S. Helms-Burton law.

"They (Denmark) agree on the principle," Brittan said. He said the Danish objection referred to the legal basis in the EU treaties on which the EU's proposals for retaliatory measures rested. EU foreign ministers had been expected to approve those proposals at a meeting next Monday.

The EU, Canada, Mexico and others have strongly attacked the U.S. Helms-Burton law which seeks to tighten the screws further on Havana by opening the way for Americans to take legal action against any foreign company investing in property confiscated in Cuba since the 1959 Communist revolution.
